name: Meta Prometheus
description: Used by: Meta. Meta Prometheus is unusual for its ad hoc construction, spanning the full length of New Albany Business Park. A combination of weatherproof tents, colocation facilities and Meta’s traditional data center buildings, this data center shows Meta’s pivot towards AI. Reflecting that patchwork, our analysis uses a combination of land use maps, natural gas turbine permitting, and satellite/aerial imagery of cooling equipment to estimate compute capacity.

name: Microsoft Fairwater Atlanta
description: Used by: OpenAI (likely), Microsoft (likely). Microsoft Fairwater Atlanta is a QTS-built data center with Microsoft as a tenant, and it likely provides training compute for OpenAI. We estimate the compute capacity primarily based on satellite and aerial imagery of the chillers, and disclosures that it contains NVIDIA GB200 GPUs.

name: Anthropic-Amazon New Carlisle
description: Used by: Anthropic. Anthropic-Amazon New Carlisle is part of the Anthropic-Amazon Project Rainier collaboration. It is similar to other Amazon locations, forgoing most external cooling infrastructure in favor of direct air based cooling.

name: Colossus 2
description: Used by: SpaceXAI, Cursor, Anthropic. Colossus 2 is the follow-up to Colossus 1. Like its predecessor, it is located in Memphis and was converted from an existing building. To start powering the data center, xAI made the unusual choice to install natural gas turbines across the border in Mississippi, possibly to get faster approval for their operation. We use a combination of satellite/aerial images and announcements to estimate the timeline and compute capacity of the data center.

controversy.summary: xAI ran dozens of unpermitted gas turbines at this Memphis site for over a year, in a majority-Black South Memphis neighborhood already burdened with industrial pollution (cancer risk ~4x the national average in nearby Boxtown). Studies link the turbines to a sharp rise in local nitrogen dioxide levels; the Southern Environmental Law Center and Earthjustice sued on behalf of the NAACP, and a U.S. Senator opened an investigation into the unpermitted operation.

name: QTS Richmond
description: QTS Richmond is a 15-building campus with an estimated total IT power over 650 MW. Construction on the first site began in 2022 and was accelerated significantly in 2024. QTS owns enough adjacent land to build two or three additional sites of the same size and has indicated to regulators that this could be a 1GW+ campus by 2030. However, further development of this area will require new power infrastructure to be built by the local grid operator, which is still in the permitting phase.

name: OpenAI Stargate Abilene
description: Used by: OpenAI. The Stargate data center campus in Abilene Texas is expected to host OpenAI's largest compute cluster from the second half of 2025 through 2026. This is the first of several sites in the Stargate project, spanning the US and the globe. We have a variety of sources to estimate the capacity of this data center, from company announcements, to permit documents, to satellite imagery of air-cooled chillers.

name: Microsoft Fairwater Wisconsin
description: Used by: OpenAI (likely), Microsoft (likely). Microsoft Fairwater Wisconsin is the tech giant’s most powerful data center yet, and likely provides training compute for OpenAI. One building is operational, with a second partly built. An expansion with 9 buildings is underway in the northwest. We estimated compute capacity based on disclosures from Microsoft, and permit applications showing the layout of server racks.

name: DayOne Nusajaya
description: The DayOne campus in Nusajaya Tech Park spans 13 buildings. We exclude the first three (Phase 1), because Phase 2 was reported to be the first in the region supporting "large-scale AI computing". Power is estimated from a synthesis of DayOne-reported numbers and Epoch AI's cooling model.

name: Colossus 1
description: Used by: Anthropic. Colossus 1 was converted from a factory into a data center in 2024. Initially, Colossus 1 was powered by portable gas turbines and a small pre-existing substation. This infrastructure has since been replaced by two additional substations providing power from the local grid, with batteries providing backup power. In May 2026, Anthropic signed an agreement with SpaceX to use the compute capacity here.

controversy.summary: xAI ran dozens of unpermitted gas turbines at this Memphis site for over a year, in a majority-Black South Memphis neighborhood already burdened with industrial pollution (cancer risk ~4x the national average in nearby Boxtown). Studies link the turbines to a sharp rise in local nitrogen dioxide levels; the Southern Environmental Law Center and Earthjustice sued on behalf of the NAACP, and a U.S. Senator opened an investigation into the unpermitted operation.

name: Google Columbus
description: Used by: Google DeepMind (likely). Google Columbus is currently a 5-building campus in Ohio. Power capacity was estimated by factoring in cooling plus a transmission line construction notice giving detailed capacity breakdowns.

name: Amazon Madison Mega Site
description: Used by: Anthropic (speculative). Amazon's Madison Mega Site is similar to other Amazon locations, forgoing most external cooling infrastructure in favor of direct air based cooling. Plausibly part of the Anthropic-Amazon Project Rainier collaboration.

name: Google New Albany
description: Used by: Google DeepMind (likely). One of several data centers in the New Albany Business Park; only buildings added or modified since 2024 are counted as AI-specific capacity.

name: Microsoft Goodyear
description: Used by: OpenAI (likely), Microsoft. SemiAnalysis reported this site was intended for OpenAI use; Microsoft has indicated its own MAI-Thinking-1 model was trained here.

name: Meta Jeffersonville
description: Used by: Meta. Announced January 2024 with an investment of more than $800 million, two primary buildings on a 619-acre site within the River Ridge Commerce Center.

name: Meta Rosemount
description: Used by: Meta. An AI-optimized campus on 280 acres of former University of Minnesota UMore Park land, more than $800 million invested.

name: Meta Montgomery
description: Used by: Meta. Began with a 715,000-square-foot campus; a September 2025 expansion will grow it to approximately 1.3 million square feet.

name: Meta Kuna
description: Used by: Meta. Shares its AI-ready design with Meta Temple in Texas. Two buildings planned to start use in summer 2026.

name: Meta Temple
description: Used by: Meta. A traditional H-shaped data center was partially built by 2023, then demolished in favor of Meta's new AI-optimized design; a third building was later added to the plan.

name: Amazon Ridgeland
description: Used by: Anthropic (speculative). Forgoes most external cooling infrastructure in favor of direct air based cooling; plausibly part of the Anthropic-Amazon Project Rainier collaboration.

name: Google Council Bluffs (East)
description: Used by: Google DeepMind (likely). Site dates to 2014; analysis focuses on buildings added to the east since 2024, similar to Google's New Albany and Omaha sites.

name: Microsoft Project Osmium
description: Used by: OpenAI (speculative). A 5-building Iowa campus; per SemiAnalysis reporting, an early building held ~25k A100s used by OpenAI to train GPT-3.5.

name: CoreWeave Chester VA
description: Chirisa secured $200M to fit out this CoreWeave-leased facility, reported as a 27MW build with a 12-year lease; broader Chesterfield JV buildout ties to larger future capacity.

name: Alibaba Zhangbei
description: Used by: Alibaba (likely). Part of China's "Eastern Data, Western Compute" project launched in 2021; Zhangbei county is favorable for abundant wind and solar power. Only capacity added since 2024 is counted as likely AI workload.

name: Google Lincoln
description: Used by: Google DeepMind (likely). A Nebraska campus expected to span 7 construction phases, currently in Phase 2.

name: CoreWeave Denton TX
description: Owned by Core Scientific, formerly a bitcoin mining facility, being repurposed to run AI on CoreWeave's GPUs; contract specifies 260 MW total dedicated for CoreWeave.

name: Goodnight
description: Used by: Google DeepMind (speculative). Crusoe's site, originally designed in 2024 to mirror OpenAI Stargate Abilene's first 8 buildings, revised in 2025 to 6 simpler buildings.

name: Google The Dalles
description: Used by: Google DeepMind (likely). Google's only large data center known in Oregon; analysis covers buildings completed since 2025 (the "3rd facility").

name: Fluidstack Lake Mariner
description: Used by: Anthropic (likely), G42 (likely). Built at a former coal plant on Lake Ontario; Terawulf-owned campus mixing crypto-mining and AI. Fluidstack's buildings reportedly serve Google TPUs for Anthropic.

name: Google Storey County
description: Used by: Google DeepMind (likely). One of the rare dry-cooled Google campuses, adapting to water-scarce Nevada; growing since 2019, now planned for four buildings.

name: Google Lancaster
description: Used by: Google DeepMind (likely). An Ohio campus with two currently operational buildings.

name: Oracle Batam
description: Built and operated by DayOne, which has a large presence in Southeast Asia; assumed filled with the latest NVIDIA Blackwell servers.

name: Google Papillion
description: Used by: Google DeepMind (likely). A 5-building buildout on a smaller 2019 Nebraska site.

name: CoreWeave Marble NC
description: Core Scientific's site, transitioned from crypto mining to dense GPU hosting for CoreWeave starting June 2024; full contracted 65 MW handed over by May 2026.

name: Google Omaha
description: Used by: Google DeepMind (likely). Google's second Nebraska site, after Papillion.

name: Microsoft SAT40
description: The newest building on Microsoft's San Antonio site and the second believed used for AI.

name: Google Mesa
description: Used by: Google DeepMind (likely). An Arizona campus with two operational buildings and visual evidence of a third under preparation.

name: STACK Infrastructure NVA02
description: A 10-building campus (6 for AI) with a future IT power capacity of 350 MW for AI; first high-density AI hall went live Q4 2024.

name: Google Midlothian
description: Used by: Google DeepMind (likely). One of Google's two campuses in the Dallas-Fort Worth area.

name: Google Red Oak
description: Used by: Google DeepMind (likely). One of two Google sites in the Dallas-Fort Worth area.

name: Stream Phoenix
description: A 7-building campus, 6 of which are planned to be AI-ready; targeting 280 MW total IT power (220 MW for AI) by 2030.

name: Microsoft SAT14
description: A fully completed 2-building campus, built in four permitted phases.

name: Vantage TX1
description: One of two known Vantage campuses in the Phoenix area; building TX11 operational, TX12 under construction, TX13 planned.

name: Start Campus Sines Data Campus
description: Used by: Microsoft. A planned six-building campus reportedly completing in 2030 with 1.2 GW of IT capacity; first building (SIN01) operational and hosting Europe's first NVIDIA GB300 chips via Nscale, for Microsoft.

name: Google Pryor (North)
description: Used by: Google DeepMind (likely). Dating to 2007, this Oklahoma site has served Google Workspace and machine learning; analysis covers buildings completed since 2024.

name: Meta Hyperion
description: Used by: Meta. Built on a tract more than three times the size of Central Park; set to host Meta's next flagship AI cluster after Prometheus, backed by Entergy gas-turbine and MISO substation filings.

name: Coreweave Helios
description: Used by: Microsoft (speculative). Retrofitted from a former Galaxy crypto-mining facility, now leasing ~800 MW of approved capacity to CoreWeave, with 2.7 GW more under study.

name: Google Cedar Rapids
description: Used by: Google DeepMind (likely). Similar to Google's New Albany and Omaha sites; permitting suggests more than twice the cooling towers per building.

name: QTS Cedar Rapids
description: Sits alongside a Google data center in Big Cedar Industrial Center; two phases expected complete late 2026 and late 2027.

name: OpenAI Stargate Shackelford
description: Used by: OpenAI. The second US Stargate site, ~20km from Abilene; developed by Vantage under the name "Frontier", first building delivery expected late 2026.

name: Google Fort Wayne
description: Used by: Google DeepMind (likely). A planned five-building campus using Google's newer, larger building design; estimated ~1 GW and 1.2M H100-equivalents when complete in 2028.

name: Crusoe Abilene Expansion
description: Used by: Microsoft (likely). Built by Crusoe, originally planned as a Stargate Abilene expansion for OpenAI/Oracle, reportedly drew NVIDIA and Meta interest before being acquired by Microsoft.

name: OpenAI Stargate Lordstown
description: Used by: OpenAI. One of five Stargate sites announced together; permitting shows plans to retrofit a former GM/Foxconn plant for data-center equipment manufacturing.

name: OpenAI Stargate New Mexico
description: Used by: OpenAI. Also known as Project Jupiter; will be powered by two microgrids, per air-quality permitting.

name: OpenAI Stargate Wisconsin
description: Used by: OpenAI. Developed by Vantage; environmental filings split the site into two projects completing Q3 2028 and later.

name: OpenAI Stargate Michigan
description: Used by: OpenAI. Developed by Related Digital; capacity ramp tied to DTE Energy permitting and Michigan Public Service Commission filings.

name: OpenAI Stargate Milam
description: Used by: OpenAI. Powered by SB Energy; TDLR filings indicate the first building completing October 2026.

name: Google Kansas City East
description: Used by: Google DeepMind (likely). A Missouri site similar to Google's Omaha and Columbus campuses; construction evidence of four buildings so far.

name: Stargate UAE (G42, Al Dhafrah)
operator: G42 / OpenAI / Oracle / SoftBank / Cisco / NVIDIA
scale: First 200 MW phase live 2026; campus planned to reach 5 GW over ~19.2 km²
description: The largest announced AI data center campus outside the United States, anchored by G42 and operated jointly with OpenAI and Oracle. First 200 MW cluster targeted for 2026; full build envisions 5 GW powered by a mix of nuclear, solar and gas.

name: Mistral AI Campus (Bruyères-le-Châtel)
scale: 44 MW initial; roadmap to 200 MW by 2027 and part of a planned 1.4-3 GW Paris-region campus by 2030
description: France's flagship sovereign-AI cluster, south of Paris, backed by a joint venture between Mistral AI, Nvidia, France's Bpifrance and Abu Dhabi's MGX aiming to build Europe's largest AI campus.

name: Stargate UK (Cobalt Park)
scale: ~8,000 GPUs offtake in early 2026, scaling toward 31,000
description: UK "AI Growth Zone" site built by Nscale. OpenAI initially committed to offtake compute here, but paused its rental in 2026 citing high UK energy costs and regulatory uncertainty; Nscale's build continues with Microsoft and Nvidia as partners.

name: Stargate Norway (Kvandal)
description: OpenAI's first announced European data center, in the Arctic Circle near Narvik to exploit abundant local hydropower. OpenAI stepped back from renting the capacity in April 2026; Microsoft is taking up the spare capacity instead.

name: Stargate Argentina (Patagonia)
description: OpenAI's first Latin American Stargate site, a letter-of-intent project with Argentine-US firm Sur Energy in southern Patagonia, framed as a $25bn investment. Exact location not yet finalized as of mid-2026, so the marker is placed at an approximate Patagonia location.

name: Reliance Intelligence AI Campus
scale: 120 MW commissioning end-2026, part of a $110B AI infrastructure commitment
description: India's largest announced AI compute campus, powered entirely by Reliance's Kutch solar platform. Meta is leasing 168 MW of capacity here for its first built-to-suit AI data center in India.

name: Stargate Korea (Southwest region)
description: SK Telecom signed an MoU with OpenAI to develop, build and operate an AI data center in southwest South Korea, part of Stargate's hardware-supply partnership with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.

name: Alibaba Zhenwu Data Center
gpu_type: Domestic chips (Alibaba self-developed + Huawei Ascend ecosystem)
description: Part of China's push toward a domestic-chip AI computing grid (a reported $295B national plan to run 80% of capacity on Chinese silicon). Alibaba's Guangdong facility runs its own chips as Chinese firms commit 500,000+ combined Huawei Ascend chip orders for 2026.
